content.overview: Statutory liability in tort arises where legislation creates a duty, standard, prohibition or statutory compensation mechanism and the legal consequences of breach are determined by the statute together with the applicable principles of tort law.
content.glance: Statutory liability in tort arises where legislation creates a duty, standard, prohibition or statutory compensation mechanism and the legal consequences of breach are determined by the statute together with the applicable principles of tort law.
content.study:
Statutory liability in tort arises where legislation creates a duty, standard, prohibition or statutory compensation mechanism and the legal consequences of breach are determined by the statute together with the applicable principles of tort law.

A statutory duty does not automatically create a private damages action for every breach. The court must construe the statute to determine the nature of the duty, the persons protected, the remedy intended by Parliament or the legislature, and whether the breach is actionable at private law. Statutory duties may also coexist with ordinary negligence or public-law remedies.

This topic is included as a dedicated Torts coverage unit so students can distinguish the doctrine from neighbouring causes of action and apply it to factual problems.

sections.heading: Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: A statutory duty does not automatically create a private damages action for every breach. The court must construe the statute to determine the nature of the duty, the persons protected, the remedy intended by Parliament or the legislature, and whether the breach is actionable at private law. Statutory duties may also coexist with ordinary negligence or public-law remedies.

sections.heading: Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Identify the statute and the exact statutory duty or liability provision. 2. Determine whether the claimant falls within the class protected by the provision. 3. Determine whether the statute creates an express remedy or private cause of action. 4. If no express cause of action exists, construe the statutory scheme to determine whether private-law liability is intended or recognised. 5. Where tort principles apply concurrently, establish duty, breach, causation and recoverable damage. 6. Distinguish private-law damages from public-law compensation or statutory compensation schemes.

sections.heading: Application and Boundaries
sections.body: Identify the precise cause of action, establish the required ingredients, distinguish related doctrines, test causation and damage, and then address defences and the appropriate remedy.

sections.heading: Current Verification Status
sections.body: The doctrine and case list require authoritative primary-source judgment verification, citation verification and later-treatment checking before publication.

examples.title: Exam illustration
examples.body: A problem question should identify whether the facts satisfy the elements of Statutory Liability and Tortious Duties, distinguish the nearest alternative doctrine, and conclude only after applying the required ingredients to the proved facts.

examples.title: Boundary illustration
examples.body: Do not treat every procedural error, statutory breach or multi-party accident as automatically establishing the same tort. Identify the precise legal basis of liability.
